newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Britain to evacuate its nationals from Albania.
newsitem.headline: Britain to evacuate its nationals from Albania.

text.p: Britain prepared on Thursday to evacuate some 120 British and other nationals from Albania by sea on a British naval vessel, an embassy spokesman in Tirana said.
British, Commonwealth and some European Union nationals were told to gather at the British embassy in Tirana in the early afternoon, bringing passports and minimum luggage.

"In view of the further deterioration of the situation in Albania and reports that the airport in Tirana is closed, we are now arranging for evacuation as soon as possible," the Foreign Office in London said in a statement.
In a message sent to British residents, the Foreign Office said: "This is a final warning, and there is no guarantee of any subsequent evacuation being arranged by civil or military means."

In Tirana, British embassy official Patrick Owens said that the original plan had been to fly people out in transport planes, but with the closure of the airport they would now seek to leave in a naval vessel via the port of Durres, 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana.
He told Reuters the Albanian government had been unable to guarantee the safety of the aircraft or the evacuees.
It was planned that the group would drive in convoy to Durres, which is closed to civilian traffic, either on Thursday afternoon or Friday morning.
"We asked for a military guard, but they were unable to provide it," Owens said.

The United States has already ordered 160 of its government employees and their families to leave Albania, where armed rebels are demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha. It has urged another 2,000 Americans to go.
